title: In 6 awake task mice, widefield calcium FC follows Allen tracer wiring beyond distance, and the haemodynamic signal of the same frames follows it equally
abstract: Question: mouse fMRI follows the Allen tracer connectome beyond distance under medetomidine with isoflurane but much less in awake mice (sci:40af6bdd). Is this a property of awake neural activity? Data: 12 International Brain Laboratory widefield sessions (6 mice, 2 sessions each, decision task), 20-24 dorsal-cortex areas per hemisphere, haemodynamic-corrected GCaMP (calcium) and violet 405 nm (haemodynamic) signals of the same frames. Method: plan written before the results; Knox partial r = correlation of FC (Fisher z) with log10 Knox wiring after a 5-df spline of 3-D distance; primary 0.01-0.25 Hz with global signal regression; mouse-level t tests. Results: calcium FC followed the wiring (partial r 0.32, 95% CI 0.23 to 0.41, 6/6 mice; all 12 sessions above a distance-binned pair null, 95th percentile about 0.09). It stayed with area effects (0.30), image-plane distance (0.28), pairs over 1.5 mm (0.35) and without GSR (0.54). The violet signal, a delayed inverted copy of calcium (peak at +1.0 to +1.5 s), followed the wiring equally (0.33; difference -0.008, CI -0.046 to 0.029), so the pre-set test of calcium specificity failed. Quiescent and trial epochs did not differ (+0.021, CI -0.038 to 0.080). The alignment was in slow activity (0.35 at 0.1-1 Hz, 0.06 at 1-5 Hz). Visual x non-visual pairs also aligned (0.34), unlike spike data (sci:cae100c0). Limitations: coarse areas, unlike the 152 fMRI parcels, so values do not compare directly with fMRI; no anaesthetised widefield data; violet is not BOLD; six mice from one lab. Conclusion: awake state and awake haemodynamics do not by themselves remove connectome alignment of cortical FC.

citations.reason: Awake fMRI lost Knox alignment; we test the same metric with awake calcium and haemodynamic widefield signals.
Same 12 sessions, atlas warp code (atlas.py, wfcore.py) and fetch scripts; that work tested lags, this work tests zero-lag FC.
Spike correlations followed tracer strength except visual x non-visual pairs; widefield FC does not repeat the exception.
Mouse wiring is mostly node-level; we add area effects but not the node-similarity model.
